'''Kazuo Nakamoto''' ({{langx|ja|中本 一男}},<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ndlsearch.ndl.go.jp/books/R100000002-I000010648342|author=|title=ベンゼン環の二色性 (Doctoral Dissertation by Kazuo Nakamoto)|publisher=NDL Search|language=ja|accessdate=2025-12-21}}</ref> 1 March 1922 - 7 June 2011) was a Japan-born American chemist and Professor Emeritus of Chemistry at [[Marquette University]]. He specialized in [[Infrared spectroscopy|infrared]] and [[Raman spectroscopy]].

== Early life and career ==
Born in [[Kobe|Kōbe]], [[Hyōgo Prefecture]], he graduated from [[Osaka Imperial University]] and joined the university as a research assistant in 1945.<ref name=USA></ref> He was promoted to a research associate in 1946, then lecturer in 1951.<ref name=USA>{{Cite book |title = American Men & Women of Science |editor=Jaques Cattell Press |publisher = R. R. Bowker Co. |edition = 16th|volume = V|year=1986| page = 604}}</ref>

In 1953, he earned his DSc from Osaka University, after which he continued to serve as a lecturer at the university for a further four years, spending the final two years as a [[Fulbright Scholar]] in the laboratory of [[Robert E. Rundle]] at [[Iowa State University]].<ref name=NLS>{{cite web|url=https://www.marquette.edu/chemistry/nakamoto.php|title=Nakamoto Lecture Series, Dr. Nazuo Nakamoto|publisher=Chemistry, Marquette University|accessdate=2025-12-22}}</ref>

He was promoted to assistant professor at Osaka University in 1957.<ref name=USA></ref> However, he moved to a research fellowship position at [[Clark University]] the same year, becoming an assistant professor there in 1958.<ref name=USA></ref><ref name=CEN>{{cite journal|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/89/i39/Kazuo-Nakamoto.html|title=Kazuo Nakamoto|journal=Chemical & Engineering News|publisher=American Chemical Society|volume=89|issue=39|date=2011-09-26|accessdate=2025-12-22}}</ref>

In 1961, he moved to the [[Illinois Institute of Technology]] as an associate professor, becoming a full professor in 1967.<ref name=CEN></ref> He then transferred to [[Marquette University]] in 1969 and became the first Wehr Distinguished Professor of Chemistry.<ref name=NLS></ref> From 1965 to 1973, he also served as a consultant at [[Argonne National Laboratory]].<ref name=CEN></ref> He retired from the university in 1991.<ref name=CEN></ref> He passed away in 2011.<ref name="CEN" />

== Research ==
He pioneered the use of infrared and Raman spectroscopy, as well as [[X-ray diffraction]], to elucidate the relationship between bonding patterns and vibrational frequencies in [[metal complexes]] and [[clathrate hydrates]].<ref name=NLS></ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nakamoto|first1=K.|first2=M.|last2=Margoshes|first3=R. E.|last3=Rundle|author3-link=Robert E. Rundle|title=Stretching Frequencies as a Function of Distances in Hydrogen Bonds|journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc.|year=1955|volume=77|issue=24|pages=6480–6486|doi=10.1021/ja01629a013|bibcode=1955JAChS..77.6480N}}</ref> His influential spectroscopy textbooks, ''Infrared and Raman Spectra of Inorganic and Coordination Compounds'', systematically contain correlation diagrams of frequency shifts in metal-ligand bonds and [[hydrogen bonds]], now known as '''Nakamoto diagrams'''.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Dulski|first1=Mateusz|last2=Marzec|first2=Katarzyna M.|last3=Kusz|first3=Joachim|last4=Galuskina|first4=Irina|last5=Majzner|first5=Katarzyna|last6=Galuskin|first6=Evgeny|title=Different route of hydroxide incorporation and thermal stability of new type of water clathrate: X-ray single crystal and Raman investigation|journal=Scientific Reports|volume=7|article-number=9046|year=2017|doi=10.1038/s41598-017-08152-1|doi-access=free|pmc=5567383|pmid=28831152|bibcode=2017NatSR...7.9046D}}</ref>

He then turned his attention to biological problems and conducted extensive research on [[Heme|heme-related compounds]].<ref name=NLS></ref>

== Awards ==
He received an [[Alexander von Humboldt Award]] in 1974.<ref name=USA></ref>

== Selected publications ==
* ''Drug-DNA interactions: structures and spectra'', 1st ed., Wiley Methods of Biochemical Analysis (2008). {{ISBN|978-0471786269}}
* ''Infrared and Raman Spectra of Inorganic and Coordination Compounds, Part A: Theory and Applications in Inorganic Chemistry'', 6th ed., Wiley Interscience (2009). {{ISBN|978-0471743392}}
* ''Infrared and Raman Spectra of Inorganic and Coordination Compounds, Part B: Applications in Coordination, Organometallic, and Bioinorganic Chemistry'', 6th ed., Wiley Interscience (2009). {{ISBN|978-0471744931}}
